title: HER3 receptor and its role in the therapeutic management of metastatic breast cancer.
relation: Review: HER3 lacks strong kinase activity and pairs with HER2 to form the most transforming ErbB dimer, driving PI3K/AKT signaling in breast cancer.

title: HER3 signaling and targeted therapy in cancer.
relation: Review: HER2 activates HER3 through heterodimerization; blocking HER2 upregulates HER3 as compensation, and a HER2/HER3/IGF-1R complex is linked to trastuzumab resistance.

title: A Comprehensive Review of HER2 in Cancer Biology and Therapeutics.
relation: Review: HER2 is the preferred heterodimer partner of EGFR, HER3 and HER4, and its downstream signaling boosts estrogen and progesterone receptor activity.

title: HER2 therapy. HER2 (ERBB2): functional diversity from structurally conserved building blocks.
relation: Review of how HER2 forms active heterodimers with EGFR and HER3 and how HSP90 binding stabilizes HER2 and limits HER2/HER3 pairing.

title: Inhibitors of HSP90 block p95-HER2 signaling in Trastuzumab-resistant tumors and suppress their growth.
relation: Full-length and truncated p95-HER2 are HSP90 client proteins; HSP90 inhibitors degrade them and halt trastuzumab-resistant breast tumor growth.

title: Hsp90 restrains ErbB-2/HER2 signalling by limiting heterodimer formation.
relation: HSP90 bound to HER2 holds back its signaling by limiting formation of HER2/HER3 heterodimers.

title: A critical role for HSP90 in cancer cell invasion involves interaction with the extracellular domain of HER-2.
relation: Cell-surface HSP90 binds the HER2 extracellular domain; blocking this contact reduces heregulin-driven HER2/HER3 activation and breast cancer cell invasion.

title: CHIP/STUB1 Ubiquitin Ligase Functions as a Negative Regulator of ErbB2 by Promoting Its Early Post-Biosynthesis Degradation.
relation: The E3 ligase CHIP/STUB1 ubiquitinates newly made HSP90-bound HER2 for proteasomal degradation, lowering surface HER2 in breast cancer cells.

title: ATM kinase sustains HER2 tumorigenicity in breast cancer.
relation: ATM stabilizes HER2 by promoting the HER2-HSP90 complex and preventing HER2 ubiquitination, sustaining AKT signaling in HER2-positive breast cancer.

title: The SH2 domain protein GRB-7 is co-amplified, overexpressed and in a tight complex with HER2 in breast cancer.
relation: GRB7 is co-amplified with HER2 in breast cancer and binds phosphorylated HER2 tightly through its SH2 domain.

title: Dissecting GRB7-mediated signals for proliferation and migration in HER2 overexpressing breast tumor cells: GTP-ase rules.
relation: In HER2-positive breast cancer cells, GRB7 couples HER2 to SHC/RAS for proliferation and to FAK/VAV2/RAC1 for migration.

title: The HER2 amplicon includes several genes required for the growth and survival of HER2 positive breast cancer cells.
relation: RNAi screen of 17q12 amplicon genes shows several genes co-amplified with HER2 (STARD3, GRB7, PSMD3, PERLD1/PGAP3) support HER2-positive breast cancer cell growth.

title: TNFα-Induced Mucin 4 Expression Elicits Trastuzumab Resistance in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.
relation: TNF-alpha induces MUC4, which reduces trastuzumab binding to HER2 and causes resistance; MUC4 predicts poorer disease-free survival in HER2-positive patients.

title: N-Acetylcysteine breaks resistance to trastuzumab caused by MUC4 overexpression in human HER2 positive BC-bearing nude mice monitored by 89Zr-Trastuzumab and 18F-FDG PET imaging.
relation: In mouse models of HER2-positive breast cancer, MUC4 overexpression blocks trastuzumab access to HER2, and N-acetylcysteine restores response.

title: Insulin-like growth factor-I receptor/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 heterodimerization contributes to trastuzumab resistance of breast cancer cells.
relation: In trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer cells, IGF-1R binds and transactivates HER2; breaking the heterodimer restores trastuzumab sensitivity.

title: Heterotrimerization of the growth factor receptors erbB2, erbB3, and insulin-like growth factor-i receptor in breast cancer cells resistant to herceptin.
relation: HER2, HER3 and IGF-1R form a three-receptor complex in trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer cells.

title: Combating trastuzumab resistance by targeting SRC, a common node downstream of multiple resistance pathways.
relation: SRC activation is a shared downstream node of several trastuzumab-resistance routes in HER2-positive breast cancer, and SRC inhibition restores response.

title: Interaction of CDCP1 with HER2 enhances HER2-driven tumorigenesis and promotes trastuzumab resistance in breast cancer.
relation: CDCP1 binds HER2 through its intracellular domain and increases HER2-SRC interaction, enhancing HER2 signaling and trastuzumab resistance.

title: PTEN activation contributes to tumor inhibition by trastuzumab, and loss of PTEN predicts trastuzumab resistance in patients.
relation: Trastuzumab acts partly by activating PTEN through SRC inhibition; PTEN-deficient breast cancers respond poorly to trastuzumab.

title: Mutant PIK3CA accelerates HER2-driven transgenic mammary tumors and induces resistance to combinations of anti-HER2 therapies.
relation: An activating PIK3CA mutation speeds up HER2-driven mouse mammary tumors and makes them resistant to combined anti-HER2 therapy.

title: PIK3CA mutations in HER2-positive breast cancer: an ongoing conundrum.
relation: Commentary on the clinical evidence linking PIK3CA mutations to reduced benefit from HER2-targeted therapy in HER2-positive breast cancer.

title: Protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B deficiency or inhibition delays ErbB2-induced mammary tumorigenesis and protects from lung metastasis.
relation: Loss or inhibition of PTP1B delays HER2-driven mammary tumors and lung metastasis in mice, so PTP1B acts as a positive regulator of HER2 signaling.

title: Beta 4 integrin amplifies ErbB2 signaling to promote mammary tumorigenesis.
relation: Beta-4 integrin forms a complex with HER2 and amplifies its signaling to STAT3 and c-Jun, driving mammary tumor onset in mice.

title: Memo mediates ErbB2-driven cell motility.
relation: MEMO1 binds the phospho-Y1227 site of HER2, likely through SHC, and is needed for HER2-driven breast carcinoma cell migration.

title: ERBIN: a basolateral PDZ protein that interacts with the mammalian ERBB2/HER2 receptor.
relation: ERBIN's PDZ domain binds HER2 directly and keeps the receptor at the basolateral membrane of epithelial cells.

title: Erbin interacts with NHERF1 and Ezrin to stabilize a membrane ErbB2 signaling complex in HER2-positive breast cancer.
relation: Erbin joins NHERF1, Ezrin and HSP90 in a membrane complex that keeps HER2 active; losing Erbin lowers HER2 signaling.

title: Estrogen/HER2 receptor crosstalk in breast cancer: combination therapies to improve outcomes for patients with hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive breast cancer.
relation: Review of two-way crosstalk between estrogen receptor and HER2 signaling and how it drives therapy resistance in HR-positive/HER2-positive breast cancer.

title: Resistance to therapy in estrogen receptor positive and human epidermal growth factor 2 positive breast cancers: progress with latest therapeutic strategies.
relation: Review of endocrine and anti-HER2 resistance in ER-positive/HER2-positive breast cancer, driven by ER-HER2 pathway crosstalk.

title: Advances in HER2-Targeted Therapies: From monoclonal antibodies to dual inhibitors developments in cancer treatment.
relation: Review of HER2 structure, its dimerization with other HER family receptors, and HER2-targeted drugs.
